target_customer: Advertisers and data buyers in sales, marketing and recruiting who need bulk company, people, jobs and technology data
problem: Advertisers could not see which display ads and traffic sources worked for competitors; MixRank indexed ad networks to show them, and later sold bulk company data feeds.
product_category: Ad intelligence, later B2B data feeds

founders.name: Scott Milliken
education: UC Berkeley, BA in Mathematics (YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he began college at 14 and has been programming since age 11.

founders.name: Ilya Lichtenstein
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in TechCrunch June and December 2011; one profile says he left in 2016 (unverified).

competitors.name: Nielsen and comScore
competitors.what: Large research firms that sell display advertising and audience measurement

technical_complexity.rationale: Crawling and indexing about 93,000 AdSense sites at launch and then ad data at scale required real data infrastructure for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated crawl history is hard to rebuild, but ad spy tools were copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied it; the company reports itself founder owned and not for sale.

market_need_then: At launch it indexed about 93,000 AdSense sites and over 4,000 advertisers built campaigns by December 2011 (TechCrunch).

branding.domain_note: Uses mixrank.com; no domain history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, founder voiced copy on the company site

brand_strength.rationale: Name was ad ranking oriented and no press about the brand or community was found.

pivots.to: Bulk company, people, jobs and technology data feeds
pivots.why: Not stated; the current site sells hourly data feeds

outcome_analysis: MixRank launched an ad intelligence tool in 2011, raised a $1.5M seed from 500 Startups and Mark Cuban, and later shifted to selling bulk company data feeds. The company says it is profitable, founder owned and not for sale, though this is self reported. No acquisition, layoffs or large rounds were found, so it looks like a small, durable data business.
notes: 2015 and 2016 $250K debt entries rest on a single database (Seedtable); amounts and dates are as shown there. The seed is stated by TechCrunch and Dallas Innovates. The Nielsen and comScore competitor entry comes from an undated page described in search results as a 2011 startup Q&A; the page was not opened. Dealroom headcount and revenue figures conflict and are not used. As of the 2011 launch there were also ad intelligence tools but no dated source named them.
